t: You're looking at a statue of the architect Sir John Soane, at the Bank of England. Soane was a bricklayer's son who rose to the top of his profession, became professor of architecture at the Royal Academy, and was knighted in 1831. The sculptor was William Reid Dick, a Scot known for simplified, stylised forms. The architect Herbert Baker designed it. Baker is remembered for his Neo-Classical work in South Africa. Soane worked in that same Neo-Classical style, which makes him a fitting figure to commemorate here.
